name: Split Cord Malformation, Composite Type

criteria.description: Presence of a bony or cartilaginous septum dividing the spinal cord
Identification of two separate dural sacs on imaging
Presence of a fibrous septum dividing the spinal cord
Associated spinal anomalies such as tethered cord or vertebral anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a bony or fibrous septum dividing the spinal cord with two dural sacs on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Composite type involves features of both Type I and Type II split cord malformations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental neurological deficit corresponding to split cord level
searchTerms: neurological symptoms affecting specific spinal segments
segmental nerve deficits matching spinal level
localized weakness or numbness at split cord level

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible or palpable midline spinal bony spur
searchTerms: visible or felt bony spur along midline spine
spastic lower limbs with muscle weakness
increased muscle tone and leg weakness

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to motor impairment
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to motor issues
gait problems caused by muscle impairment

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: bladder problems like retention or leakage

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hairy patches or dimples over the spine
searchTerms: skin signs like hairy patches or dimples on back
hairy or dimpled skin spots on back

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to the site of malformation
searchTerms: localized back pain at malformation site

occasional.symptomName: Sensory disturbances including numbness or paresthesia

rare.symptomName: Hydromyelia or syringomyelia associated with split cord
searchTerms: syrinx or hydromyelia in spinal cord

rare.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome with progressive neurological decline
searchTerms: tethered spinal cord causing worsening symptoms
progressive neurological decline from cord tethering
spinal cord stuck causing nerve problems
bowel control problems from nerve damage
difficulty with bowel movements due to nerve issues

imaging: MRI demonstrating split spinal cord with bony or fibrous septum
CT scan showing bony spur and vertebral anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence common
other: Physical examination revealing midline spinal deformity or cutaneous markers

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of bony or fibrous septum dividing the cord
Progressive neurological symptoms without split cord
Open neural tube defect with exposed neural tissue
No distinct split cord with two dural sacs
Associated with skin defects or meningomyelocele

redFlags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Sudden onset of severe back pain with neurological deterioration
references: Mahapatra AK, Gupta DK. Split cord malformations: a clinical study of 254 patients and a proposal for a new clinical-imaging classification. J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2005.
Pang D. Split cord malformation: Part I: A unified theory of embryogenesis for double spinal cord malformations. Neurosurgery. 1992.
